Role Summary
About the role
We are seeking an experienced and proactive Senior Network Infrastructure Engineer to join our Information Services department and play a key role in delivering and supporting critical IT infrastructure across the British Museum.
This is an excellent opportunity for an established infrastructure professional with strong networking expertise who enjoys combining hands-on technical work with operational oversight. Working within a small and collaborative technology team, you will help ensure the stability, security and performance of our network services, supporting colleagues across the organisation to deliver important public and charitable outcomes. In addition, you will provide functional leadership across infrastructure operations, taking ownership of service quality, monitoring workloads, overseeing ticket queues and driving issues through to resolution.
This is an opportunity to use your technical expertise in an organisation where technology directly supports an important public mission. You'll join a supportive team environment and play a significant role in maintaining and improving critical services that enable our colleagues to deliver meaningful outcomes for the communities we serve.
If you're an experienced infrastructure professional with a strong networking background who enjoys taking ownership, driving improvements and ensuring excellent service delivery, we'd love to hear from you.

About us:
Our mission is to provide transformative, high-quality digital education, so students can learn, wherever they are.
We collaborate with academics and professional services staff across the university, and with our external partners, to design, develop and deliver a wide range of educational programmes. Our learners study with us from across the world, choosing when and where they study, working around their schedules.
We are a dynamic team with ambitious growth targets in a priority area of development for King’s: online distance education. We proudly foster a supportive culture and community which prioritises both individual and collective wellbeing.
Employee support at King’s includes flexible working arrangements, paid maternity/shared parental leave, menopausal support, an active wellbeing programme, training and development opportunities and much more. All of our staff benefit from a generous pension contribution as well.
As part of King’s hybrid working, all team members can work remotely for part of the week if they wish.
Join us as we open futures and unlock potential.

Head of Digital Products and Experience
Can you shape the digital transformation of one of the UK's most visited museum groups?
About us
The Science Museum Group (SMG) is a world-leading cultural organisation, welcoming millions of visitors each year to the Science Museum in London, the Science and Industry Museum in Manchester, the National Railway Museum in York, Locomotion in Shildon, and the National Science and Media Museum in Bradford.
Digital is changing how people discover culture, plan visits and connect with meaningful stories. At SMG, this creates an exciting opportunity to make our collections more accessible, relevant and engaging through audience-first digital experiences.
Over the next four years, we will bring our websites, online collections and museum experiences together into a more seamless digital journey, expanding our reach, boosting commercial resilience and building the skills and responsible AI practices needed to innovate with confidence.
We are seeking a Head of Digital Products and Experience to develop SMG's goal for a more connected digital experience across our sites. This is a full-time role (35 hours per week) and can be based at any Science Museum Group site.
The role currently works to a hybrid working pattern, which offers flexibility to work from home. There will be a requirement to travel between our sites with frequent travel to London as this is where a majority of the team sit.

Schools Learning Producer
About us
Royal Museums Greenwich is a collection of diverse historical sites. The sites are the National Maritime Museum, Cutty Sark, the Royal Observatory, and the Queen’s House. Each of these sites has a unique identity and a common purpose to serve our communities, through sharing our collections and expertise. We are a place to explore the sea, space, art and history, and our strategy ‘Charting Our Course’ puts people at the core of its success.
The Role
If you are passionate about the role Museums play in the learning journeys of children and young people, then this is the role for you. We are looking for a dynamic individual to work with schools and teachers to support and inspire collections-based learning at the National Maritime Museum and the Queen’s House. You will lead on the development, delivery and resourcing of historical enquiry programmes from early years to post 16, giving all school learners a high-quality experience that is unique to our sites. You will also nurture relationships with key internal and external stakeholders, ensuring that audience voice is embedded into everything we do.
The successful candidate will have a proven track record of engaging children and young people using museum collections and a great understanding of the needs of school learners and teachers. Effective time management and written and verbal presentation skills are also required. This role involves working with histories relating to empire and the transatlantic trade of enslaved people so experience of culturally sensitive approaches to exploring these topics is essential. It’s a fast-paced and rewarding role that puts learning at the centre of the Museum.
